drivingQuestion: Does the mishna imply that gift recipients etc. cannot establish presumptive ownership?
outcomeNote: the answer (חסורי מחסרא) follows in the next unit

segments.he: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים – בְּמַחְזִיק, אֲבָל בְּנוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה וְהָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ וְכוּ׳. אַטּוּ כֹּל הָנֵי דְּאָמְרִינַן, לָאו בְּנֵי חֲזָקָה נִינְהוּ?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «In what» case «is this statement,» that one establishes the presumption of ownership after profiting from the property for a certain duration, «said?» It is said «in» a case of one who «has» mere «possession» of the property, which does in some cases serve as proof of ownership. «But in» a case of one who «gives a gift, or brothers who divided» their inheritance, or one who takes possession of the property of a convert who died without heirs and his property is now ownerless, as soon as one locked the door of the property, or fenced it or breached its fence even a bit, this is considered taking possession of the property, and effects acquisition. The Gemara asks: «Is that to say» that «all of these whom we» previously «said» possessed the field for three years «are not subject to» the halakhot of «taking possession» of property in this manner?

moves.summary: mishna: presumption of three years applies to a possessor, but gift/division/convert's property acquire by locking, fencing, breaching
are all these not subject to the presumption of ownership?
moves.about: the mishna's contrast implies that gift recipients, dividing brothers and convert's-property takers are not subject to the three-year presumption
